As with DataFrame.assign(), later arguments can refer to columns computed earlier in the same call (GH 61522, GH 40322). df = pd.DataFrame( ... { ... \"first_name\": [\"John\", \"Alice\", \"Bob\"], ... \"last_name\": [\"Smith\", \"Cooper\", \"Marley\"], ... \"age\": [61, 22, 35], ... } ... ) df.select(\"first_name\", \"last_name\") first_name last_name 0 John Smith 1 Alice Cooper 2 Bob Marley df.select(\"first_name\", pd.col(\"age\"), age_months=pd.col(\"age\") * 12) first_name age age_months 0 John 61 732 1 Alice 22 264 2 Bob 35 420 df.select( ... \"first_name\", ... age_months=pd.col(\"age\") * 12, ... age_days=pd.col(\"age_months\") * 30, ... ) first_name age_months age_days 0 John 732 21960 1 Alice 264 7920 2 Bob 420 12600 Filtering with a boolean mask in DataFrame.filter and Series.filter# DataFrame.filter() and Series.filter() now accept a boolean mask through the new cond keyword, keeping the rows (or columns with axis=1) where the mask is True. cond may also be a callable returning a boolean mask or an expression created with pandas.col(); these two forms may also be passed positionally, which is convenient in method chains (GH 61317). In : df = pd.DataFrame({\"a\": [1, 2, 3], \"b\": [4, 5, 6]}) In : df.filter(cond=df[\"a\"] > 1) Out: a b 1 2 5 2 3 6 In : df.filter(pd.col(\"a\") > 1) Out: a b 1 2 5 2 3 6 In : df.filter(lambda df: df[\"b\"] < 6) Out: a b 0 1 4 1 2 5 A Series mask is aligned with the filtered axis; any other mask must have the same length as that axis. Missing values in the mask are treated as False by default, matching obj[mask] for a mask with nullable boolean dtype. Pass na=True to keep the corresponding entries instead, or na=\"raise\" to raise. In : mask = pd.array([True, None, False], dtype=\"boolean\") In : df.filter(cond=mask) Out: a b 0 1 4 In : df.filter(cond=mask, na=True) Out: a b 0 1 4 1 2 5 Any other value passed positionally continues to select labels, as before.
